chapter_outcomes: Marketing to achieve enterprise aims which included increasing consumer awareness of the enterprise, product (good or service), establishing and maintaining brand loyalty, increasing or defending sales, market share or profit
Marketing from the perspective of customers which including greater knowledge of the enterprise, product (good or service), the ability to make more informed decisions
Methods of identifying potential customers via primary and secondary research

Analyse the effectiveness of different methods for enterprises by evaluating their advantages and disadvantages in terms of cost, availability, suitability for the enterprise and target market, and other context-specific factors.

The methods of measuring customer satisfaction and retention including: number of sales and complaints, mystery shopper feedback questionnaires, focus groups
Methods of retaining existing customers including effective customer service, resolving complaints, loyalty rewards, new products and services

Methods of marketing communication to reach intended customers including television, radio, cinema, newspapers and magazines, posters, leaflets, online communication and social media, word of mouth and announcements, sponsorship

Evaluate and select appropriate methods for different enterprises by analysing their advantages and disadvantages in terms of cost, availability, suitability for the enterprise and target market, and other context-specific factors.
